newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU hints at support for Saudi barley offers.
newsitem.headline: EU hints at support for Saudi barley offers.

text.p: Offers to sell Spanish, French, German and British barley to Saudi Arabia at a price equivalent to slightly higher than $140 a tonne fob Gulf would be seriously considered, European Commission sources said on Wednesday.
"Serious offers of around $25 a tonne above U.S. maize would stand of good chance of being covered (by EU export restitutions)," a source said.
The source was commenting on a Saudi tender to buy 1.2 million tonnes of feed barley for January and February shipment.
"It would be silly to miss such a good export opportunity," the source said, adding that the barley might otherwise end up in intervention stores at much greater cost to the EU budget.
Brussels is prepared to push barley sales to Saudi Arabia although freezing weather and strong demand for malting barley have increased tightness on the EU market.
At least 800,000 tonnes could come from the EU, including unusually Spanish barley after an excellent crop following several years of drought.
Buyers seeking prompt deliveries were running into transport problems due to frozen canals and ports in northern Europe, sources noted.

European exporters also had to contend with rising freight rates, which for 75,000-tonne vessels sailing from Dunkirk, a major French export port for Saudi Arabia, had recently risen by $10 a tonne to $24 a tonne, they said.
Barley is unusually more expensive than maize which is currently priced at $116 to $118 a tonne fob U.S. Gulf for Jan/Feb shipment.

It was uncertain whether the result of the Saudi tender would be known before European exporters submitted bids for export refunds at the weekly EU grain tender on Thursday, the first for three weeks due to the Christmas holidays.
But traders were still expected to test the Commission's flexibility over export subsidies.
